minden-minden-1885-07-21.A1: One hundred mounted, armed men, entered the town of Minden, La., on the night of July 21st, and killed two negroes confined in the jail there. They took prisoner every citizen who appeared on the scene; among the prisoners was Mr. Moses Fort, editor of the Democrat Tribune. Fearing attack, probably, they concluded to "Hold the Fort," which they did for several hours when he was turned loose.
minden-minden-1885-07-21.A2:
South and West.
JOHN DANIELS, of Mount Junction, Ill., was married the other morning and killed in the afternoon by his father-in-law, who had opposed the match.

CHARLES JACKSON, who lives in the mountains of West Augusta, Va., in a frenzy of rage dragged his child from its cradle and dashed out its brains. He then knocked down his wife and fled.

GOVERNOR MARTIN, of Kansas, has issued a proclamation providing for the prevention of the importation of infectious cattle into the State.

A CAR containing soldiers on their way to Asheville, N. C., to attend the first encampment of State troops held in the South since the war, was overturned ten miles from Asheville. Fourteen men were wounded, four of them seriously, but none were killed. Train loads of visitors were present in Asheville, from Tennessee, Georgia, South Carolina, North Carolina and Virginia, and the whole city was decorated.

A CROWD of men forcibly entered the jail at Minden, La., and shot to death two colored prisoners accused of murder.

JOHN FAUGMAN, his wife, and three-year-old son have died in Baltimore from trichinosis.

THE prospects of the cotton crop in Texas surpass those of the great crop season of 1883.

SEVEN negro train hands were killed by the ditching of a train at Suwanee, Ga.

A BOX expressed from Black River Falls, Wis., to Chicago excited the suspicions of the express messenger, and was opened at Elroy, Wis. Inside was a man, heavily armed and with a bottle of chloroform and stout cords. He had evidently intended to rob the express car at some convenient point.

Washington.

The President has appointed William H. Moffett, of New Jersey, an Episcopal minister, to be consul at Athens, and John Devlin, of Michigan, to be consul at Windsor, Ont. Mr. Devlin has been assistant labor commissioner of Michigan.

SECRETARY MANNING has sent out a circular inviting from manufacturers and others their views as to the feasibility of simplifying the tariff and making the duty specific, so as to protect home industries.

The President has appointed Samuel H.uck to be postmaster at New Orleans; Benjamin E. Russell, at Bainbridge, Ga.; William H. Dawley, at Antigo, Wis.

A PROCLAMATION has been issued by the President directing the cattlemen in the Cheyenne and Arapahoe reservation, in the Indian Territory, to remove their cattle within forty days.

ADDITIONAL postmasters appointed by the President: Frank P. Crotzier at Nanticoke, Penn.; Simon Sawyer at Fairmount, Neb.; George C. Rembaugh at Winfield, Kansas; Geo. F. Laskell at Laramie, Dak.; Thomas B. Crawford at Grand Junction, Col.; Frank Shutt at Litchfield, Ill.; George J. Spohn at Superior, Neb.; W. E. Lewis at Chariton, Iowa; William A. Fleming at Nashua, Iowa. John Dawe at Edgerton, Wis.; Wm. B. Alexander at Pine BuiT. Ark.; S; R. Davis, at Creston, Iowa. Richard Sinnot, surveyor of customs, at the port of New Orleans. Collectors of customs, Peter F. Coghill, district of Petersburg, Va.; Benjamin R. Tate, district of New London, Conn.; Bradley B. Smalley, district of Vermont; Theodore D. Jersey, district of Charleston, S. C.; Oliver Kelly, district of Perth Amboy, N J.

The President has referred charges made against the recently appointed Postmaster Jones, of Indianapolis, Ind., to the civil service commission, and Commissioner Thoman and Chief Examiner Lymon have gone to Indianapolis to investigate the matter. It is charged that Postmaster Jones violated the civil service rules in discharging employees. THE total values of the imports of merchandise during the twelve months ended June 30, 1885, were $577,476,850, and during the previous twelve months, $667,697,693, a decrease of $90,229,843. The values of the exports of merchandise for the twelve months ended June 30, 1885, were $741,893,683, and for the twelve months ended June 33, 1884, were $740,513,609, an increase of $1,380,074.

minden-minden-1885-07-21.A6:
GENERAL NEWS.
Secretary Whitney has decided that the eight-hour law shall hereafter be enforced in the different navy yards; that is, the employees shall receive ten hours' pay for eight hours' labor. Heretofore they received eight hours' pay for eight hours' labor. The general order directing the change has not been issued yet, but information of the proposed change has been received at the Washington navy yard.

C. C. Warner & Co. forwarded to-day by fast freight, 10,000 pounds of general merchandise for Tuscaroa.

The law officer of the Postoffice Department has given an opinion to the effect that a Postmaster who uses or converts to his own use postal funds in his possession, though not required to deposit them till the end of each current month or quarter, is guilty of embezzlement.

Sacramento is being flooded with bogus silver dollars.

A fire in Eureka Cal., Wednesday night destroyed property to the value of $1,200.

Most of the vineyardist about Orange, Cal., have disposed of their raisin crops. Numerous cases of glanders are reported in Oregon and Washington Territory.

It is estimated that an outlay of $50,000 will construct the projected irrigating canal near Modesta, California.

Spokane, W. T., has issued $50,000 worth of bonds for the purpose of constructing water works.

Sixty bales of hops from the White River country, Washington Territory, have been shipped to Cincinnati O.

After mature consideration, the President and Cabinet have reached the conclusion that the lands of lands in Indian Territory held by cattle men are invalid and it has been determined to take steps to have them set aside.

Samuel Porcher, a mormon, is under arrest at Salt Lake City for marrying his niece as his sond wife.

The Puget Sound stamer Wildwood was burned to the water's edge at Olympia, W. T., on Tuesday. Loss about $14,000.

The Sacramento Evening Sun is the latest aspirant for public favor in the journalistic field of California.

One hundred armed men forced open the door of the Minden, L.C., jail Tuesday night and proceeded to where were confined two notorious negro desperadoes, Cleero Green and John Figures, fired at them in their cell until they filled them both with buckshot and then departed.

Mr. Moffett, who has been appointed United States Consul to Athens, is an Episcopalian minister. He was recently appointed Consul to Beirut, Turkey, but the appointment was withdrawn at the request of the Turkish Minister, who said a Consul who is a msnister was not wanted.

Most extraordinary assays have been made at the Smithsonian Institute at Washington, of a score or more specimens of silver ore recently discovered in Polk county, Tennessee. The assays average $220 per ton. The said vein extends throughout thousands of acres, and the report has created great excitement.
Whales were eaten by people of the upper class in Europe as late at least as the thirteenth century. The tail and tongue, dressed with peas, or roasted were prized as choice delicacies. The Princess Eleanor de Montiford paid, in 1265, the sum of 24s for "100 pieces of whale" to be used as food in her household.

Charles Koening, a draughtsman, and Frederick Rich, a machinist, fought a duel with pistols, at Marshall's Hollow, ninety miles from Pittsburg, Wednesday morning. Two shots were exchanged. At the first fire neither party were hit, but at the second, Koening received a ball in the side, inflicting perhaps a fatal wound. Warrants have been issued for both principals. Jealousy was the cause of the meeting. Rich has disappeared.

The Commission inquiring into the mental condition of James McUllough, has renamed a verdict that "McCulough is a lunatic, and has been so for the space of six months last past, but enjoys some lucid intervals, yet is incapable of managing his person or estate." The schedule places the value of his real estate at $200 and his personal property at $44,304. The Court will probably appoint the Guarantee Trust and Safe Company as committee of the estate and Wm. F. Johnson, as committee of the person.

The Reno papers say that County Surveyor Bridges, of Washoe, with a party of seven men started for the Oregon line Wednesday, to return the excitement.

From Shreveport.
Special to the Commercial Herald.
SHREVEPORT, Aug. 1—Henry Jackson, colored, who killed and robbed R. A. Britton, saloon keeper, at Minden Junction, about a week ago, and was caught at Arcadia and jailed at Minden, was brought here to-night for safe keeping. After incarceration at Jackson he acknowledged the crime and the rumor prevailed he would be lynched, hence his removal here, the people of Minden desiring to evade another lynching in their town like that of a few days ago.
